criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Mission (GBR coral monitoring via fluid lensing), rationale, single-spacecraft justification and users/operator/funding all addressed with literature references. Detail is good though some claims lack depth.

evidence.quote: Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: All major requirements addressed: Vega E from Kourou, SSO elements table, manoeuvres, Mt Pleasant station, STK access report, 5-year duration, drag-sail EOL. Errors: contradictory altitude/resolution statement, garbled EOL text, no hand calculations shown, STK files not evidenced.

evidence.quote: an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924°
Systems Tool Kit 11 (STK) was used to calculate access periods
A span of five years is a sound estimate

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusions summarise each segment and note risks (Vega E availability), but remain largely a recap without quantitative outcomes or recommendations.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure and headings; executive summary present. But figures lack numbered captions, bibliography is bare URLs including Wikipedia (unacceptable per task), and some sentences are garbled/contradictory.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Contradictory statement: 'A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable' – low resolution is not desirable.
Contradictory/garbled: satellite 'without thrusters' yet discusses uncontrolled retro-burn descent; drag-sail sentence is incomplete ('to ‘ and is suitable').
Wikipedia used as a source, explicitly disallowed; references are bare URLs without titles/authors/dates.
Justification relies on a Feb-2021 calendar extrapolated to 2025; Vega E selection is speculative and alternatives only briefly noted.

overall: A well-structured, mostly complete mission design for GBR reef monitoring with STK evidence and all major requirements addressed. Weakened by internal contradictions, incomplete EOL discussion, unnumbered figures, and non-compliant referencing (Wikipedia, bare URLs).

feedback.summary: A well-structured, mostly complete mission design for GBR reef monitoring. Your introduction is strong and all major mission-design requirements are addressed with STK evidence. To reach the top band, resolve internal contradictions (altitude/resolution, EOL), complete the drag-sail discussion, add hand calculations and STK files, number your figures, and replace Wikipedia/bare-URL references with proper citations.
next_steps: Fix the contradictory statement in the Orbit section: low-resolution imagery is not desirable for reef monitoring; restate the altitude trade-off clearly.
Complete the Mission Duration & EOL section: resolve the 'without thrusters' vs retro-burn contradiction and finish the incomplete drag-sail sentence.
Replace Wikipedia and bare URLs with full references (authors, titles, dates, access dates) and ensure in-text citations match the list.
Add numbered figure/table captions (e.g. 'Figure 1: STK 3D view of orbit') and include STK files or hand calculations as evidence in the body or appendix.
Strengthen the launch justification beyond the Feb-2021 calendar extrapolation and briefly compare Vega E against alternatives.
Deepen the conclusion with quantitative outcomes and recommendations rather than a recap.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (8/10). Your introduction clearly presents the GBR fluid-lensing mission, its rationale, the single-spacecraft justification and users (CSIRO, BOM). To reach the very top, deepen some claims with more detailed discussion and additional literature support.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (7/10). All major requirements are addressed: Vega E from Kourou, SSO elements (600 km, 97.7924°), manoeuvres, Mt Pleasant station, STK access analysis, 5-year duration and EOL. The next level requires error-free content (fix the altitude/resolution and EOL contradictions), shown hand calculations, and STK files/screenshots presented as clear evidence.
criteria.C3: Adequate (6/10). Your conclusion summarises each segment and honestly flags the Vega E availability risk, but it reads largely as a recap. Higher marks require conclusions drawn from your evidence: quantitative outcomes (e.g. access statistics, coverage) and specific recommendations.
criteria.C4: Adequate (5/10). Structure, headings and executive summary are good, but figures lack numbered captions, the bibliography uses bare URLs and disallowed Wikipedia, and some sentences are garbled. The next level requires consistent, professional formatting and fully compliant referencing.
